title: Nine years on the Madison, no band union, then nursing training and Detroit
summary: Nine years on the Madison plus extra jobs, then she left for nursing in Chicago and played in Detroit.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Do you remember a boat called the Camellia? What?
The Camellia. I don't think that's the name of the South Camellia. I might have heard but I don't know. I never did play on it I know. No?
You just played the one time on the Capitol?

Yeah on the Capitol. Because I was on the Schema Madison for nine years. And then playing around other extra jobs. Sometimes I'd be off from the boat and then I'd go play. Sometimes we'd go to Ocean Springs or something like that, you know, Laura, Mississippi, play one job or two jobs. Different bands. I played all the bands around here. What about, where were you when beer came back? When beer? Came back, you know, after Prohibition. Right here in New Orleans. Yeah. Right here in New Orleans. What about when hard liquor came back? Right here in New Orleans. I see. Right here in New Orleans. See I used to go away but I'd come back. Oh I see. I went to Chicago. That's where I started my first training in Chicago, nursing. And I left there after I put in a year there and finished and got an approval from there for nursing. Then I left there and came back to New Orleans. Then I stayed in New Orleans for a few months. I got a job playing there with a band and I said well I'll stay here because I'm going on to New York to finish up my schooling. So I stayed there in Detroit for about two months. And we didn't have the union there. They only had like a club there where all the musicians would meet there. It's called the Band Box Club. This was in Detroit?
